messages:
Anna C: Hey — noticed a cluster of reconnects from EU edge that show up as "failed" in the console and immediately decrement tenant quota. Seen this only on streaming (SSE) paths since yesterday. Anyone else? :eyes:
Kevin L: I saw that too briefly this morning. Any correlation with the proxy rollout?
Anna C: Possibly. Console trace points to proxy returning 204 w/o last-event-id and then client reconnects. Console code path treats reconnect without resume id as a new session and charges.
Matt B: Sounds like sticky routing + resume token scrub. If resume token is missing we should try to rehydrate from session cookie before counting as new, or at least not decrement quota until auth re-check.
Julia P: UX question — users are seeing a billing drop in the route-level dashboard. We should avoid noisy alerts for canary edge nodes. Maybe add a suppressor for duplicate short reconnects (<5s) in console counts.
Anna C: Repro steps attached (minimal):
```
# client opens SSE
GET /v1/stream?model=foo
Accept: text/event-stream
Cookie: session=sess123
# proxy returns 204 early
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
# client reconnects immediately without Last-Event-ID
GET /v1/stream?model=foo
```
We treat the second GET as a brand new session and bill.
Kevin L: Can you paste the proxy access log lines? need trace ids.
Anna C: paste: `proxy-eu-2 172.16.4.5 - [13/Mar/2026:08:04:12 +0000] "GET /v1/stream?model=foo" 204 - "-" "curl/7.85" trace=tr-9a2` and then `proxy-eu-2 ... "GET /v1/stream?model=foo" 200 - "-" "curl/7.85" trace=tr-9a3`
sre-bot: alert: streaming-reconnects-eu spike (5xx-like reconnects) — triggered 8:04 UTC — investigation channel #incidents
Matt B: The key is distinguishing graceful 204 drains vs opaque proxy midstream closes. We already have a resume-id header when resume is intended: `X-Resume-Id: <id>` — if missing, fallback to cookie rehydrate AND apply short grace window to avoid double-billing.
Julia P: For console telemetry: add a tag `reconnect_cause=proxy-early-eof` and a metric `reconnect_billing_suppressed` for the grace window so product can see suppressed vs real charges.
Kevin L: Proposed patch: proxy adds `X-Proxy-Resume: none|forwarded` and runtime changes counting to `if (resume_present || cookie_rehydrated || within_grace_window) { no-bill } else { bill }`. Canary to 10% eu-edge first.
Anna C: 👍 I'll draft change and set up a canary. Who can own the runtime-side guard? @Kevin L?
Kevin L: I can own runtime guard, will open PR and link to this thread. Plan: patch, unit tests for three cases, canary 10% eu-edge, monitor `reconnect_billing_suppressed` and route-level charges for 24h.
Julia P: I'll add a console annotation and temporary alert mute for the canary nodes.
Matt B: Also update docs (rollout notes) and add a migration entry in the console changelog to explain suppressed counts.
Anna C: Thanks all — moving to action. Tagging: @sre-bot keep watch on spike and mute noisy alerts. :thumbsup:
